games.title: Plural Patrol
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to understand basic grammar appropriate to the language being studied, including (where relevant): feminine, masculine and neuter forms and the conjugation of high-frequency verbs; key features and patterns of the language; how to apply these, for instance, to build sentences; and how these differ from or are similar to English
games.instruction: Read it carefully, then tap True or False.
games.hint: Not quite. Most nouns just add -s, but some words change more. Try again.

questions.ask: To make most French nouns plural, you add -s.
"le chat" becomes "les chats" in the plural.
"la pomme" becomes "la pommes" in the plural.
"le gâteau" becomes "les gâteaux" in the plural.
"l'oiseau" becomes "les oiseaus" in the plural.
The -s at the end of "chats" is usually silent.
"les" is used for both masculine and feminine plural nouns.
"un cheval" becomes "des chevals" in the plural.
"le nez" stays "les nez" in the plural, because it ends in z.
